# Implement the Music System defined by the Audio Design Chapter

## Goal

Build the runtime background-music system for AI Hell against the fixed design contract captured in
`docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` (produced by **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)**).

User story: *As a player, I want a dynamic, retro-arcade soundtrack that responds to combat intensity, so
that runs feel like the relentless survival experience the game is aiming for; and as a developer I want the
music engine driven by a documented parameter/state contract, so behaviour is testable and reproducible.*

> **Scope stance:** this is **future scope, out of MVP** (GDD §8). The MVP ships baked ToneForge SFX only
> (GDD §7.3), and §7.3 remains authoritative for SFX. This item must **not** be started until the design
> chapter exists and has been reviewed, and it must **not** promote music into the MVP without an explicit
> producer decision.

## Background

- AI Hell currently has **no background music** by design: GDD §7.3 keeps music out of MVP scope, and the
  player-fire grid is deliberately quantised to a **silent internal 80 BPM beat** (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).
- SFX are build-time baked WAV assets rendered deterministically by ToneForge and played through Phaser's
  shared `AudioContext` (`src/audio/effects.ts`); the authoritative cue catalogue is
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`.
- The Audio Design Chapter specifies the musical identity (Phrygian Dominant combat scale, Lydian ambient
  scale, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), instrumentation palette, dynamic-mixing rules, state-driven
  transitions, parameter mapping, audio budget and accessibility requirements.

## Expected behaviour and outcomes

- A music system that plays layered/stemmed music driven by an explicit game-state parameter, with
  bar-boundary transitions, stingers, and ducking, as specified by the chapter.
- Music state follows gameplay (e.g. menu/attract, wave combat, boss, low-health tension, run end) with the
  transition rules and timings given in the chapter, and never disrupts the beat grid or the SFX mix.
- Reproducible, deterministic behaviour suitable for automated tests; no audio regressions to the shipped SFX
  pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Contract traceable to the chapter:** every implemented music state, transition, stinger and mixing parameter traces to a named section of `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`, recorded in a mapping table in the implementation docs.
- [ ] **AC2 — Musical content matches the documented identity:** the delivered cues/stems use the chapter's scales, motifs and progressions (Phrygian Dominant combat, Lydian ambient, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), verified by an explicit audit table (motif → scale degrees → usage state).
- [ ] **AC3 — State machine implemented and tested:** transitions occur only at the documented boundaries (bar boundaries unless a stinger cut-in is specified), with unit tests covering each transition in the chapter's transition matrix, including invalid/reset paths.
- [ ] **AC4 — Dynamic mixing implemented:** ducking, per-layer volume targets and the priority tiers behave as specified; SFX intelligibility is preserved (music ducks under key SFX cues) and is covered by tests.
- [ ] **AC5 — Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.
- [ ] **AC6 — Budget met:** the shipped music respects the chapter's audio budget (memory, streaming, polyphony, layer count) on the supported targets, measured and recorded.
- [ ] **AC7 — Docs updated:** GDD §7.3 and §8 are updated to reflect the shipped music system, and `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` is marked as implemented for the sections that ship.
- [ ] **AC8 — No SFX regression:** the existing ToneForge baked-SFX pipeline and cue catalogue remain unchanged and their tests pass; any chapter §6.4 procedural SFX recipes are explicitly **not** adopted unless decisioned separately.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project build and test suite pass.**

## Constraints

- **Blocked by** the docs item **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — this item
  must not begin before `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` exists.
- Music stays **out of MVP scope** until a producer decision promotes it (GDD §7.3, §8).
- Keep the gameplay SVG/vector aesthetic and retro-arcade palette of the chapter; UK English in all docs.
- §7.3 (baked ToneForge SFX) remains authoritative for SFX; the chapter is an addendum whose §6.4 procedural
  SFX recipes are design reference only.
- Prefer reusing the existing audio plumbing (`src/audio/effects.ts`, shared `AudioContext`, manifest-driven
  playback) over introducing new runtime dependencies; any middleware adoption (the chapter's FMOD/Wwise
  guidance) is a separate decision — the web build currently has no middleware.

## Approach (indicative)

1. Confirm scope with the producer (MVP vs post-MVP) and record the decision on this item.
2. Ingest the chapter into an implementation mapping table (state → parameter → cue/stem set → transition).
3. Decide the delivery mechanism (baked stems via ToneForge + `AudioContext` playback, per the existing
   pipeline) versus a runtime synthesiser; record the trade-off before coding.
4. Implement the music state machine and mixing layer behind a single facade, mirroring the existing SFX
   façade style; add unit tests per transition and per mixing rule.
5. Add accessibility controls and the autoplay guard; verify budget and measure on target hardware.
6. Update GDD §7.3/§8 and the chapter's implemented-sections marker.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` — the design contract (prerequisite)
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — existing SFX façade / shared `AudioContext` plumbing to reuse
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — where combat-state music parameters would be driven from
- `src/core/rules.ts` — game-rules config (including `beatBpm`) that music tempo must stay coherent with
- `src/audio/` — new music module + tests
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 and §8 updates

## Risks & assumptions

- **Overlap with the shipped silent beat grid (medium):** player fire is quantised to an internal 80 BPM beat.
  Music must be tempo-coherent with that grid or the two will fight; assume music tempo is either locked to
  `beatBpm` or documented as intentionally independent.
- **Chapter/SFX divergence (medium):** the chapter's §6.4 procedural SFX recipes differ from the shipped baked
  catalogue; §7.3 stays authoritative (AC8).
- **Middleware assumption (low):** the chapter's FMOD/Wwise guidance is forward-looking; no middleware exists in
  the web build, so it is design intent only.
- **Scope creep into MVP (medium):** music is out of MVP; promotion needs an explicit producer decision.

## Related work

- **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — prerequisite; produces the design contract.
- discovered-from:AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W
- GDD §7.3 (SFX, authoritative for MVP), GDD §8 (Future Scope — "Background music"), and
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (SFX cue catalogue).
- Beat grid / timing context: AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B (beat-aligned fire grid), AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3 (beat-timed
  explosion accents).

## Problem

`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` `_resolve_implementation_order()` builds its in-degree count from **every** in-chain dependency edge, including edges whose blocker is **already terminal** (`completed`/`in_review`/`done`). A terminal blocker therefore still occupies a slot in Kahn's ready queue and gates when its dependents become ready.

## Observed impact (2026-10-23, epic AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S)

The epic's 8 children were ordered as:

`[TOOK(test-failure, done), 3X5M, MVIS(done), VDA9, 7NGZ, O53Z(done), K0V4, BAAN]`

because `K0V4` (juice impl, sortIndex 3000 — the *lowest* open child) has an outbound 'depends-on' edge to `O53Z` (its test-first contract child, sortIndex **8100**). Since `O53Z` was already `completed`, `K0V4` should have been ready immediately, but the sort only released it after `O53Z`'s turn near the end of the queue.

Consequences observed:

1. `implement.py parent AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S` never reached `K0V4`, even though its worktree contained a completed in-flight implementation — it returned 'start child VDA9' instead. The in-flight work had to be finished manually with `implement.py finish K0V4`.
2. The reported order is not 'blockers first' in any intuitive sense: a ready child was deferred behind unrelated children purely because its (finished) blocker had a high sortIndex.

## Expected behaviour

Terminal blockers must not gate readiness: a child whose in-chain blockers are all terminal is **ready**, regardless of where those blockers sort. Suggested fix: exclude terminal blockers from `in_degree` (treat them as already satisfied) — or collapse them out of the graph before the sort — so the ready queue is ordered by `(sortIndex, id)` over genuinely-unblocked children.

## Acceptance criteria

- A child whose in-chain blockers are all terminal is ordered by its own `sortIndex`, before non-ready children and irrespective of its blockers' `sortIndex`.
- A regression test in the implement-skill test suite covers the exact shape seen here (open child with low sortIndex depending on a completed child with high sortIndex) and asserts the open child is first in the resolved order.
- No change to cycle detection, cross-project external-blocker reporting, or the blocked-child guard.
- Existing implement-skill tests pass.

# Limit the number of power-up slots

**Headline:** Cap the run's permanent loadout at six slots shared across power-ups *and* weapons; the first six distinct kinds taken as permanent rewards define the run, and once all six slots are full only those kinds (plus flagged always-available entries such as Extra Life and Mystery UFO) may spawn or be offered as a new permanent pick. Field pickups never consume a slot.

## Original request (verbatim)

> Currently the player can collect any number of powerups. This makes them way too powerful in late game. Limit the number of power-ups that can be collected to 6. The first 6 collected permanently (i.e. from the hull-full) become the only powerups the player can collect in that game. Once the 6 slots are full with permanent items no other powerup kind will spawn (a life powerup is an exception, there may be other exceptions later in the development cycles, so availability when full should become a flag on the powerup database entry). Until all 6 slots are full powerups will spawn as they do now.

> **Terminology:** the item text says "hull-full"; the shipped feature is the **hold-full choice** (`MineralChoiceScene`, driven by the mineral hold — GDD §4.5). This brief treats "hull-full" as "hold-full", i.e. a **permanent reward** grant. "Collected permanently" means a hold-full (or mini-boss reward) grant, never a field pickup.

## Problem statement

Players can currently collect every power-up and weapon kind in the catalogue, and every hold-full (permanent) reward can add a brand-new kind with no upper bound. By the late game a player therefore owns every permanent effect at once, which makes the ship far too powerful and flattens the difficulty curve. The run needs a bounded loadout: **six permanent slots shared across power-up and weapon kinds**. The first six distinct kinds the player takes as permanent rewards fill the slots; once all six are full, no other kind spawns or is offered as a new permanent pick, except kinds explicitly flagged as available-when-full (Extra Life and Mystery UFO today). Until the slots are full, spawning is unchanged.

## Users

- **Player (arcade run)** — wants a strong but bounded loadout, so late-game runs stay challenging and each run has a recognisable build identity; a drop on screen must still be worth catching.
- **Producer / designer** — wants the cap data-driven, with per-entry exemptions (Extra Life, Mystery UFO today; more later) needing no code change.
- **Agent / developer** — needs one shared implementation so the game and every gym behave identically (gym↔game parity).

### Example user stories

- As a player, once I have taken six permanent rewards my build is fixed for the rest of the run, so my late-game ship is strong but no longer invincible.
- As a player with six full slots, the only drops I see are the six kinds I chose (plus Extra Life and Mystery UFO), so every pickup improves something I own.
- As a designer, I can mark a catalogue entry as available-when-full, so a future exception is a data change, not a code change.
- As an operator, I can observe the identical slot rule in the gyms as in the shipped game.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Cap and shared accounting** — A single named, exported cap (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`) governs permanent ownership; occupied slots equal the count of **distinct permanently-owned drop kinds** — power-up ids with at least one permanent grant (`PowerUpLevelStore.getLevels()` / `permanentGrants()`) plus weapon drop ids with a permanent level ≥ 1 (`Player.getWeaponLevels()`), i.e. one shared pool of six. Field-pickup stacks never consume a slot; the permanent cannon and the `reset` utility are never counted (they cannot be permanently granted). A unit test proves the accounting: six distinct permanent grants fill the pool, a repeat grant of an owned kind levels it up without consuming a new slot, a permanent weapon grant consumes one, and temporary field stacks of either family consume none.
2. **Spawn gating at full slots** — When all six slots are filled, the drop-selection path (game and gyms, one shared implementation) draws only from the six owned kinds plus every catalogue id flagged available-when-full (Extra Life and Mystery UFO are flagged by default); every other power-up *and weapon* id is never drawn. Verified by a seeded/injected-rng unit test on the selection helper plus a `PlayScene` integration test that fills the slots and asserts a large sample of draws contains only owned/exempt ids.
3. **No behaviour change below the cap** — While fewer than six slots are filled, drop selection covers the full catalogue exactly as today: a regression test with a fixed rng seed produces the identical draw sequence before and after the change (power-ups and weapons alike).
4. **Choice gating at full slots** — Once the slots are full, the hold-full choice (and the mini-boss reward, which reuses the same option builder) offers level-ups of owned items, available-when-full entries and nothing else that would create a seventh permanent kind; the candidate list degrades gracefully (level-up options still offered) and never returns a new non-exempt kind. Verified by choice-pool tests at 6 filled slots, covering both power-up and weapon offers.
5. **Data-driven exemption** — The exemption is a flag on the power-up catalogue entry (`availableWhenSlotsFull`, default `false`), not an `id === '…'` special case; Extra Life **and** Mystery UFO set it. A test asserts both are exempt, that every other catalogue entry defaults to non-exempt, and that a newly added entry is non-exempt unless it opts in. (No weapon exemption exists today; the flag stays power-up-only until a weapon needs one.)
6. **Parity and run scope** — The rule lives once in shared core code consumed by `PlayScene` and the formation gyms (guard: `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` / parity tests); slot state is run-scoped and resets on run restart (`PowerUpLevelStore.reset()` / `Player.resetWeaponLevels()`). A parity/integration test proves the gym path and the game path consume the same gate.
7. **Documentation and suite** — The GDD (§4.4 catalogue table and §4.5 hold-full choice) and `docs/BALANCING.md` document the shared six-slot cap and the exemption flag; the full project test suite passes with the change.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1):** the rule must be implemented once in shared code (`src/powerups/*`, `src/scenes/core/*`) and consumed by `PlayScene` and the gyms. A gym may only diverge for a documented, disabled-feature reason — none is expected here.
- **Single counter, derived from existing stores:** no new slot counter. Slot occupancy is derived from the two permanent-grant stores (`PowerUpLevelStore`, `Player._permanentWeaponGrants`), so existing level semantics stay the only source of truth.
- **Existing level semantics unchanged:** a repeat grant of an already-owned kind still levels it up (field pickup = temporary level, permanent reward = permanent level).
- **Determinism:** selection must stay injectable-rng deterministic; no wall-clock or `Math.random()` reads inside the new pure helpers.
- **No catalogue removals and no weight retuning:** the cap gates which ids may be drawn, not relative weights. `GameRules.powerUpWeights` / `weaponWeights` keep their meaning for the ids that remain eligible.
- **No individual rebalancing:** the six-slot cap is the balance change; per-item power tuning is out of scope.

## Existing state

- **"Power-up database":** `src/powerups/types.ts` — `PowerUpEntry` / `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` (16 power-ups); `POWER_UP_WEIGHT_IDS` (power-ups) and `WEAPON_WEIGHT_IDS` (weapon drops) in `src/core/rules.ts`; `WEAPON_DROP_IDS`/`CHOICE_POOL` list weapon drops alongside.
- **Permanent ownership (power-ups):** `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `PowerUpLevelStore.collect(id, permanent)`, `permanentGrants(id)`, `getLevels()` (permanent kinds only) and `getEffectiveLevel`/`getTempStacks` for temporary pickups.
- **Permanent ownership (weapons):** `src/entities/Player.ts` — `equipWeapon(id, permanent)`, `getPermanentWeaponLevel(id)`, `getWeaponLevels()` (permanent kinds only), `getTempWeaponStacks`; `resetWeaponLevels()` on run restart. The cannon can never be permanently granted (`isTimedWeapon` guard) and `reset` is not a `WeaponId`.
- **Game spawn path:** `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_maybeDropPowerUp()` rolls the level-resolved drop chance, then spawns `this.dropSpawner.next()`. The spawner is built once by `buildDefaultDropSpawner()` (`src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts`) as a `WeightedRandomSpawner<DropId>` over `POWER_UP_WEIGHT_IDS + WEAPON_WEIGHT_IDS`, with weights from `src/core/rules.ts`. A small asteroid also rolls an additive deterministic `extra_life` drop.
- **Gym spawn paths:** `GymFormationScene._spawnPowerUpDrop()` (`powerUpSpawner`), `GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpLeveling`, `GymWeapons`, `GymLevel` — deterministic round-robin spawners.
- **Hold-full choice:** `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `CHOICE_POOL`, `buildChoiceCandidates()`, `drawWeightedWithoutReplacement()`, `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT`; `chooseOptions()` is consumed by `PlayScene` and every gym, and the mini-boss reward reuses `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions()` (`src/powerups/unlocks.ts`).
- **Effects application:** `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect()` routes a collection to the power-up store's temporary stack or permanent grant; `Player.equipWeapon(…, permanent)` records weapon grants. No cap on distinct kinds exists today.
- **Docs of record:** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 (catalogue/table) and §4.5 (hold-full choice), `docs/BALANCING.md` (drop/choice balance), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 (parity convention), `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`.

## Desired change

- Add `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6` and an `availableWhenSlotsFull` flag on `PowerUpEntry` (Extra Life `true`, Mystery UFO `true`).
- Add a pure shared helper module (e.g. `src/powerups/slots.ts`) that, given the permanently-owned power-up ids, the permanently-owned weapon drop ids and the catalogues, answers: slots used, slots free, and whether a drop id may be drawn/offered. It owns the shared-pool and exemption rules — no `id === '…'` branches anywhere else.
- Apply that helper at the two decision points, both shared with the gyms:
  1. **drop selection** — the weighted draw excludes non-owned, non-exempt ids once the pool is full, for power-ups and weapons alike;
  2. **choice candidate construction** — `buildChoiceCandidates` excludes base entries that would create a seventh permanent kind once the pool is full, while owned level-up offers, exempt entries and the remaining candidates survive.
- Keep the below-cap path byte-for-byte equivalent in distribution (eligible set unchanged, weights unchanged).
- Cover with unit tests (helper + spawner + choice), integration tests (`PlayScene`), gym parity coverage, and documentation updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/types.ts` — add `availableWhenSlotsFull?: boolean` to `PowerUpEntry`; set `true` on `extra_life` and `mystery_ufo`; document default `false`.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6` (mirroring existing `POWER_UP_*` constants).
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` *(new)* + `src/powerups/slots.test.ts` — pure shared-pool accounting and eligibility (power-ups + weapon drops, exemptions included).
- `src/powerups/spawner.ts` — let a draw consult an eligibility predicate (or accept an eligible-id set) without weakening the all-zero-weight fallback.
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts` — a shared `drawNextDrop(spawner, slotState)` seam (built on `buildDefaultDropSpawner`) so every scene draws through one filtered path.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — pass the run's permanently-owned power-up and weapon ids into the drop draw (keep the asteroid `extra_life` path untouched).
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — gate brand-new non-exempt kinds out of `buildChoiceCandidates` at the cap (owned level-ups and exempt entries remain).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` / `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` / `src/entities/Player.ts` — expose the owned-permanent-kind view consumed by the two gates (no new counter).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — consume the same filtered draw path (no divergent copy).
- Tests: `src/powerups/slots.test.ts` (new), `src/powerups/spawner.test.ts`, `src/powerups/choice.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (parity guard).
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 catalogue table + §4.5 choice), `docs/BALANCING.md`, `README.md` if it states power-up/weapon rules.

## Related work

- AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P — *As the levels progress increase the number of enemies and decrease the number of power ups* (level-resolved drop chance; the supply-side counterpart of this demand-side cap).
- AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X — *Add level-scaling module and tunable rules* (where `powerUpDropChanceAtLevel1/Max` live; candidate home for a tunable cap).
- AH-0MV8GPGBL009M0D8 — *Smart Bomb is too powerful* (precedent for a single-item dominance fix; this item fixes dominance by accumulation instead).
- AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 / AH-0MUV5CLVQ006V9HR — power-up level curves and the `GymPowerUpLeveling` parity gym (the permanent-grant model this cap counts).
- AH-0MUTPEIZ5002FIJP — *P10 power-up identity — catalogue, spawn pool, choice pool and icon* (established that spawn pool and choice pool are catalogue-derived; the cap must not break that invariant).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — gym↔game parity convention + duplicate-body guard.
- AH-0MVL9P2SF009QFON — shared level-up option builder used by hold-full choice and mini-boss reward (the choice gate must be applied at the shared builder seam, not duplicated).
- AH-0MUCST4M7008O9CX — *Pluggable power-up choice strategy and permanent-effect support* (the `ChoiceStrategy` seam the choice gate extends).
- AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV — *Feature: Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling* (permanent weapon-grant semantics; weapons now share this item's slot pool).

## Risks and assumptions

- **All-zero-weight fallback:** `WeightedRandomSpawner` falls back to the first entry when every weight is zero, so exclusion must not be implemented by zeroing weights — it must be an eligibility filter applied before/while sampling.
- **Empty eligible set:** if all six owned kinds are currently unofferable and no exemption applies, the eligible set must never be empty; the draw must degrade to exempt/weapon entries rather than crash or always return one id.
- **Shared-pool starvation (design consequence):** because weapons share the six slots, a weapon-heavy build can consume the pool before any power-up reward is taken. This is the producer's chosen semantics (Q1 answer (c)); the docs must state it so it is not later mistaken for a bug. Balance evidence may need re-recording (out of scope).
- **Weapons granted by other permanent paths:** mini-boss unlocks/upgrades that set a permanent weapon level ≥ 1 also occupy a slot (derived from the same store); a document + test should pin that behaviour so the pool cannot be over-filled silently.
- **Test churn:** `src/core/rules.test.ts` and `src/powerups/choice.test.ts` assert the catalogue-complete pool; those assertions need an explicit "below cap" context.
- **Bot/balance evaluation drift:** `src/ai/eval/*` simulates campaigns and will see a different late-game loadout; re-recording bot evidence is *not* in scope unless a gate fails (record as a linked follow-up if needed).
- **Scope-creep risk:** HUD slot readout (`N/6`), persisting slots in checkpoints/saved runs, capping the mini-boss weapon unlock pool separately, and rebalancing individual power-up/weapon strength are out of scope; each becomes a linked work item rather than extra scope here.
- **Assumption (A1, resolved by Q1 answer (c)):** one shared pool of six across power-up and weapon kinds; field pickups excluded.
- **Assumption (A3):** no new player-facing HUD/UX surface is required by this item (producer did not request one; if wanted, it becomes an explicit AC or a linked item).
- **Assumption (A4):** the cap is a named code constant (default 6), not a persisted `GameRules` setting.
- **Assumption (A5):** the cap applies in the gyms as well as the game (parity); no gym is exempted.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — What consumes a slot?** *Answer (producer):* **"c, field pickups are excluded"** — one shared pool of six across power-up *and* weapon kinds; temporary field-pickup stacks never consume a slot. **Resolved:** slots = distinct permanently-owned drop kinds (power-up permanent grants + weapon permanent levels), derived from the existing stores; no new counter. Source: interactive producer reply on AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF.
- **Q2 — Does the hold-full choice also stop offering new kinds at the cap?** *Answer (producer):* **"a"** — yes, the choice is gated too: at six filled slots it offers level-ups of owned items and available-when-full entries only, never a new non-exempt kind (mini-boss reward inherits the same gate through the shared option builder). **Resolved.** Source: interactive producer reply.
- **Q3 — Exemption flag and drops already on screen?** *Answer (producer):* **"a (Mystery UFO can also have the flag true)"** — the flag is `availableWhenSlotsFull` on the power-up catalogue entry (default `false`), set for **Extra Life and Mystery UFO**; drops of non-owned kinds already on screen when the sixth slot fills remain collectible for their temporary effect and simply stop spawning. **Resolved.** Source: interactive producer reply.
- **Assumption A3 (recorded, not contradicted):** no new HUD slot readout is required — if the producer wants an `N/6` indicator it becomes an explicit AC or a linked follow-up item.
- **Assumption A4 (recorded, not contradicted):** the cap ships as a named constant rather than a persisted `GameRules` field.
- **Assumption A5 (recorded, not contradicted):** gyms obey the same cap (parity).
- **Research note:** duplicate-work check performed (`wl search` on "powerup slots limit", "powerup cap", "power-up limit", "spawn pool", "hold-full choice pool", "too powerful", "power creep") — no item (open or completed) implements a permanent loadout cap, so this item is not a duplicate. Closest completed work is the level-scaled power-up *supply* reduction (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P) and the Smart Bomb power reduction (AH-0MV8GPGBL009M0D8); both are related, neither covers loadout breadth.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV** – Feature: Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling (completed)
- **AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6** – Make weapons both cumalative and time out (completed)
- **AH-0MV5CB6KO0079N08** – Remove the Power Pellet power-up from the game (completed)

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, 0muv5clvq006v9hr, 0mv8gpgbl009m0d8, 0mvht1m6o003pu7p, 0mvl9p2sf009qfon (+504 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mugzdtfx004rbd1, 0mvht1m6o003pu7p, accept, accounting, add (+433 more)

## Plan: decomposition (plan skill, 2026-10-25)

Effort/risk pre-check returned `decision: plan` (effort Small, risk Medium); the plan-approval gate returned `request_approval: false` (approval is requested only for Extra Large effort **and** High/Severe risk), so no approval pause was needed. The brief's own Appendix already carried producer answers Q1–Q3, so no new questions were required.

**Phasing (vertical slices, test-first).** Every phase is a test + implementation pair so each slice is reviewable end-to-end; the docs phase closes the item. Between phases the next item's description is re-read and updated against what actually shipped.

|---|---|---|---|

data.title: Limit the number of powerup slots

data.description: Instead of offering a choice of 5 random power ups the mini-boss rewards should be a guaranteed upgrade of an existing powerup. The UI for this will be the spin of a wheel. The wheel with have the icons of all the powerups that the player currently has in permanent slots. They will click to spin the wheel and it will spin, eventually stopping with a pointer on a given power-up. The animation for this should build tension with it spinning fast at fist then slowing. The player should not be 100% sure which icon it will land on until it stops. There will be one bonus slot, that has a special bonus icon. If it lands on this one then all existing powerups will be upgraded. Actually, thinking about it lets also have some that have 3 (randomly selected) and 2 (randomly selected) icons. So we have 100 slots, 1 has a bonus (everything upgraded), 5 have 3 powerup upgrades, 10 have 2, the rest have 1. If the player only has 1 permanent powerup then the 3 and 2 will upgrade it 2 and 3 levels.

1. branch-policy enforcement (blocks `main`/`master`/`HEAD`),
2. the context-budget regression gate,
3. `wl sync`.

No test command is executed. Consequences observed while implementing AH-0MVLJF886009584F:

- `git config core.hooksPath` is `.githooks`, and neither the committed hook nor `.git/hooks/pre-push` mentions `run_tests`.
- A push to `dev` therefore succeeds with a red or untested tree, so the documented "full suite is enforced at the dev-push gate" invariant does not hold.
- The post-push read-only verification step (`run_tests.py --summary --suite all`) returns `missing` for the pushed HEAD because the hook never populated the per-repo test cache; agents must then run the full suite manually, which (under concurrent sessions) has repeatedly failed with `slot_busy` (TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2, 600 s lock timeout).

- A push to `dev` (and `main`) runs the full suite via the test-skill runner on the pushed tree and fails the push when red, populating the per-repo test cache so post-push verification and audits can read the green entry.

- Hook runtime stays within the repo's `timeoutPerCommand` (3600 s in `.pi/test-config.json`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `.githooks/pre-push` runs `run_tests.py --scope full` (test-skill runner, not an ad-hoc command) on dev/main pushes and exits non-zero on failure.
- A deliberately failing test blocks a push to `dev` in a manual verification recorded on this item.
- The per-repo test cache contains a green full-suite entry for the pushed commit, so `run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` reports a green scope rather than `missing`.
- `docs/dev/` (release process / implement-skill reference) describes the actual gate behaviour.
- Slot-contention behaviour is documented: a gate that cannot acquire a test slot must fail the push with an actionable message rather than silently passing.

## Problem statement

The PlayScene integration test `PlayScene — Robotron homing horde (AH-0MV01EKTL001NRE6) > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`) failed once during the AI_Hell full suite (heavy machine load) and passed on a fresh full-suite re-run minutes later with identical code. It is a flaky test, not a gameplay regression, and it is the last remaining kill test in this file that has not been hardened against non-deterministic scene state.

## Users

- **AI agents and producers running the full suite** — a red full-suite gate blocks `dev` pushes and triggers `test-failure` triage items and retries.
- **Developers of the Robotron horde (and shared kill seam)** — they need the horde kill/accounting contract to stay proven while the test stays stable.

Example user stories:

- *As an agent whose `implement.py finish` gate runs the full suite, I want the Robotron horde kill test to pass deterministically so that an unrelated docs-only change is never blocked by it.*
- *As a maintainer, I want the wave-accounting contract (a horde kill counted exactly once) still asserted, so the fix does not hide a real regression.*

## Existing state (evidence)

Failure from the `implement.py finish` gate for AH-0MVLJFCE6007T77H (docs-only change, cannot affect kill behaviour):

```
FAIL |integration| src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — Robotron homing horde > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once
AssertionError: expected true to be false // Object.is equality
 ❯ src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6168:26
    6166|     scene.spawnPlayerBullet(victim.x, victim.y, 0, 0);
    6167|     scene.tick(0.001);
    6168|     expect(victim.alive).toBe(false);
```

Same run also printed repeated `connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3000` on stderr (unrelated noise; no test failed on it).

The current test body (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6174-6184`) is:

```ts
const victim = liveGrunts(scene)[0];
scene.spawnPlayerBullet(victim.x, victim.y, 0, 0);
scene.tick(0.001);
expect(victim.alive).toBe(false);
expect(wm.enemiesAlive).toBe(total - 1);
```

Two facts narrow the cause:

1. **The test is non-deterministic per run, independent of load.** `bootWithHordeWave()` never injects an RNG or run seed, so `PlayScene._initRunSeed()` draws a fresh `randomSeed()` (`Math.random()`, `src/core/rng.ts`) each run and the horde plan (`computeHordeSpawns`, `src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts`) places the 16 grunts at RNG-jittered points along the four arena edges. The passing re-run therefore re-drew a different layout; "passed on re-run" is *not* evidence that load is the variable.
2. **The identical scenario has already been fixed one describe-block earlier.** `killing a pursuer advances wave accounting exactly once` (Pac-Man pursuer) had the same single-`tick(0.001)` shape and the same flake, and was fixed by wrapping the kill in the existing module-level `isolateEnemyForKill(scene, victim)` helper (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:397-410`, documented as AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK): it stubs `getEnemyEntities()` to the victim only and disables auto-fire for the duration, so "auto-fire or an overlapping pursuer cannot add a second kill and double-decrement the wave accounting". The Robotron horde kill test is the *unhardened sibling* of that test — it predates/omits the isolation.

The description's original hypothesis ("the physics/collision step for that tick may not process the new projectile before the assertion") is **not** supported: `scene.tick(dt)` is a synchronous call that runs the full player/auto-fire/bullet/collision/accounting pass in one go (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1265+`), so a longer tick cannot make a pass "complete"; what changes with a longer tick is *how much extra state* (auto-fire bullets, homing movement, wave timer) participates in that pass.

## Diagnosis to confirm during implementation

Confirm the exact mechanism before changing the assertion. Candidate mechanisms, in order of likelihood:

1. **Auto-fire / other-bullet interference** — the scene's auto-fire is live in this scenario, so a shot fired in the same tick can hit a grunt (or a different, overlapping grunt) and shift which entity the spawned bullet resolves against. The pursuer precedent (AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK) fixed exactly this with `isolateEnemyForKill`.
2. **Overlapping horde grunts** — grunts in one spawn group share an edge and can be placed close enough that a bullet placed on the victim is also within an earlier-iterated grunt's hit radius.
3. **Wave-phase/`paused` gating** — a wave-timeout transition switches `tick()` to the carried-survivor-only collision pass (`_handleCarriedSurvivorCollisions`), and a paused scene makes `tick()` a no-op; either would leave the victim alive. Check `scene.isTransitioning()` / `paused` under the failing seed.
4. **Wall-clock frames before the loop is stopped** — `bootScene()` resumes the live RAF loop, and `advanceGame()` stops it only after a microtask yield, so real frames with real deltas run before the deterministic stepping begins (load-dependent state drift). Relevant if the failure reproduces without seed isolation.

Reproduce deterministically (seed sweep): inject a fixed seed via `scene.setRng(createSeededRng(<seed>))` before `scene.restart()` and sweep seeds until the failure reproduces, then fix and verify that seed. Prefer the narrowest fix that removes the interference.

Steps to reproduce (seed sweep):

1. In `bootWithHordeWave()`, add `scene.setRng(createSeededRng(seed))` before `scene.scene.restart()` (import `createSeededRng` from `../core/rng`).
2. Loop seeds (e.g. `0..999`) in a temporary harness or repeated test-skill runs until `victim.alive` is `true` after the kill step; note the seed.
3. Record the seed and the observed mechanism on this work item, then apply the fix and re-verify that seed plus a broader sweep.

## Desired change

Make the horde kill test deterministic **without weakening what it proves**:

- Isolate the kill exactly as the pursuer test does — reuse `isolateEnemyForKill(scene, victim)` (`auto-fire` off, only the victim visible to the collision pass) — and/or pin the scene RNG to a fixed seed so the horde layout is reproducible.
- Keep the single-tick kill if it is deterministic after isolation; otherwise use a small bounded "tick until the victim dies" loop (guard counter, e.g. ≤ 20 frames of `0.016`) and assert the *outcome*.
- Still assert that the victim dies **and** that wave accounting drops by exactly one — and, to prove "exactly once", assert the accounting is unchanged after further ticks (no double decrement).

## Acceptance criteria

- The flaky failure is reproduced deterministically first (fixed seed and/or a temporary repeat-run harness), and the observed mechanism is recorded as a comment on this work item with the failing seed (or an explicit statement that no seed reproduces it, with the evidence gathered).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — Robotron homing horde > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once` passes on repeated runs: at least 20 consecutive runs of `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` via the test skill, and at least one run with an additional concurrent load-generating job active, all green.
- The test still proves the contract: the victim grunt is dead after the kill step, and `wm.enemiesAlive` is exactly `total - 1` (and stays `total - 1` after further ticks — a kill is never counted twice). The "exactly once" proof is not weakened to "at most once".
- The fix is confined to test code (plus test comments); no gameplay behaviour, RNG semantics, or `isSpawning`/collision logic changes. If investigation shows a genuine gameplay defect is being masked, stop and record it as a new work item (`discovered-from:AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU`) rather than loosening the test.
- If the fix pattern is reusable (e.g. other horde/pursuer kill tests), note it in the test comment referencing AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU and AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK so the next reader sees why the isolation is required.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Test-execution policy:** every agent-initiated test run goes through the test skill (`/skill:test`, `run_tests.py`) — no ad-hoc `vitest`/`npm test`. Repeated-run verification is therefore a test-skill invocation with a narrow scope (changed-scope gate) plus the full-suite gate at push.
- **No assertion weakening:** a longer tick alone is acceptable only if it is deterministic after isolation; it must not become a "sleep until it works" loop with an unbounded guard.
- **No production-code behaviour change:** the horde kill path (`_resolvePlayerBulletsVsEnemies`, `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`) is shared with every gym (`src/scenes/core/`), so a behavioural change would require gym-parity work — out of scope unless a real defect is found.
- Prefer reusing existing helpers (`isolateEnemyForKill`, `finishSpawnSequence`) over introducing a new pattern.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — horde kill test at ~6174; `bootWithHordeWave`/`releaseHorde` helpers at ~6089-6124; existing `isolateEnemyForKill` helper at ~397-410 to reuse.
- `src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts` — RNG-driven spawn placement (`computeHordeSpawns`) explaining per-run layout variance.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `planHordeSpawns` / `_releaseDueHordeSpawns` (~2164-2245), `tick` collision/phase ordering (~1265-1390), `_initRunSeed` (~4849-4863).
- `src/core/rng.ts` — `randomSeed()` / `createSeededRng()` (`Math.random`-seeded runs by default).
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` — `bootScene`/`advanceGame` deterministic harness (frame-loop stop/resume behaviour).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `_resolvePlayerBulletsVsEnemies` (~1189) and `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy` (~384) — read-only context for the interference analysis.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** no gameplay defect is being masked. If the isolated test still fails for a fixed seed, the flake may reflect a real horde/accounting bug — escalate as a new (child) work item instead of widening the tick.
- **Risk:** adding `scene.setRng(...)` in this describe block changes the RNG stream for the other four horde tests in the same block; keep the seed pinned in a `beforeEach`-style helper or per-test so assertions like "spawns the configured horde" stay valid.
- **Risk:** a bounded tick loop can hide a regression that makes kills take longer; keep the bound small (≈ 0.32 s simulated) and assert exactly-once accounting afterwards.
- **Risk (scope creep):** other single-tick kill tests in the same file (asteroids, boss phases) use `tick(0.016)` and have not flaked; do not refactor them wholesale — record as separate work if desired.
- **Risk:** flake attribution — a green re-run under load is weak evidence; the fix must be justified by a *reproduced deterministic* failure, not by "it passed 20 times".
- **Risk:** `isolateEnemyForKill` stubs `getEnemyEntities` and `autoFireEnabled` on the instance and must be restored in a `finally` block (as the pursuer test does); a leaked stub would silently affect later tests in the same file.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK** (completed) — `[test-failure] PlayScene — flaky wave-accounting kill tests (Harvester + Pac-Man pursuer)`; introduced `isolateEnemyForKill` for exactly this interference class. Direct precedent.
- **AH-0MUNVVWWC0015JTM** (completed) — `Flaky tests: PlayScene and GymFormationScene fail intermittently under full-suite parallel load`; load-sensitivity remediation (deterministic boot/frames).
- **AH-0MV5JRAH90034PKR** (completed) — `Flaky Centipede chain bounds assertion under full-suite load`; fixed "advanced 20 s in one tick" by stepping in 0.05 s increments — precedent for tick-size fixes in this file.
- **AH-0MVFPMT4P005UHZL** — removed the last wall-clock waits from the suites (`advanceGame` / `stepGameUntil`); the deterministic harness this test relies on.
- **AH-0MV01EKTL001NRE6** — the Robotron homing horde feature these tests cover.
- **AH-0MVLJFCE6007T77H** (completed) — docs-only change whose gate surfaced this flake (`discovered-from`).
- `src/test/wallClockWaitGuard.test.ts` — repo guard documenting the flake history and the supported deterministic replacements.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (agent consideration):** "Is the failure load-induced (wall-clock frame drift) or seed-induced (random horde layout)?"
  - **Answer (resolved from repo evidence, no producer input needed):** seed-induced is demonstrable from the code — `bootWithHordeWave` injects no RNG, so `_initRunSeed()` draws `randomSeed()` per run and `computeHordeSpawns` places grunts at RNG-jittered edge positions. The pass-on-re-run therefore used a different layout. Load may additionally drift scene state via live RAF frames before `advanceGame` stops the loop, but that is not required to explain the flake. Source: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:4849-4863`, `src/core/rng.ts:49`, `src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts` (`computeHordeSpawns`).
- **Q (agent consideration):** "Does the description's proposed fix (`scene.tick(0.05)` / tick-until-dead) actually address the mechanism?"
  - **Answer (resolved from repo evidence):** only partially. `scene.tick(dt)` is synchronous, so "the collision step did not process the projectile" cannot happen; the pursuer precedent (AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK) shows the real interference was auto-fire / overlapping entities, fixed by `isolateEnemyForKill`. The brief therefore requires isolation (plus a fixed seed) as the primary fix, with a bounded tick loop only as a secondary robustness measure.
- **Q (agent consideration):** "Should the fix change gameplay code (e.g. horde collision ordering)?"
  - **Answer (resolved from repo constraints):** no. Any gameplay change is shared with every gym and would require gym-parity work; a genuine defect would be filed as a new work item instead. Assumption recorded in *Risks & assumptions*.
- **Producer input:** none required — the item's goal and acceptance criteria are unambiguous and the remaining decisions are resolved by repo evidence and precedent. Recorded here for auditability; no open questions.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUJRVYWG006NJUU** – Shared multi-hit kill finalisation (completed) — the shared kill seam this test's bullet path runs through.
- **AH-0MUIGTRFY002JDDS** – Shared mineral kill-drop helper + PlayScene/BaseEnemy refactor (completed) — touches the same enemy-kill finalisation path.

### Repository file matches
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — gym↔game parity convention (§5.1), relevant to the "no behaviour change" constraint.
- `src/test/wallClockWaitGuard.test.ts` — documents this flake family and the supported deterministic replacements.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — `isolateEnemyForKill` helper (AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK) reused by the fix.

## Goal

## Goal (tracer-bullet vertical slice)

Ship the first end-to-end music slice: the menu/attract ambient track ("Star Drift", Lydian) played through the existing shared AudioContext, driven by a minimal music state machine, with the autoplay/gesture guard and an independent music volume control.

This slice cuts through every layer — baked asset, playback facade, state machine, scene wiring, settings, tests, docs — so later slices extend a proven path rather than a horizontal layer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The menu/attract state plays the baked "Star Drift" Lydian ambient stem as a seamless loop.
- [ ] Music starts only after a user gesture, honouring the AudioContext resume discipline (GDD 7.3), and reuses the single shared AudioContext owned by the playback provider.
- [ ] Music volume and mute are independent of SFX and persisted in the settings record.
- [ ] The state machine enters and leaves the menu/attract state only at a bar boundary of the shared beat clock.
- [ ] Unit tests cover stem looping, the gesture guard, independent volume routing and the menu/attract transition; all playback degrades to a safe no-op without an AudioContext.

- [ ] Covers parent AC5: **Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.

1. Bake the "Star Drift" ambient stem via the ToneForge pipeline and add it to the cue/stem manifest (smallest slice of the stem pipeline).

3. Wire gesture-driven start/resume through MenuScene using the shared AudioContext.

# Shard Swarm — fire/impact VFX & SFX

**discovered-from:AH-0MVCRC52P001YIPW** (5 net-new weapon types) — audit of the `shard_swarm` player weapon found it shipped with an in-flight bullet look only: no fire sound, no muzzle flash and no per-weapon impact feedback.

## Current state (audit evidence)

Present:
- In-flight identity: `bulletShape: 'shard'` + overrides (`bulletShapeLength: 1.6`, `bulletTrail: 1.2`, `bulletSize: 0.72`, lime `BULLET_COLORS.shard_swarm = 0xc0ff33`) in `src/utils/weapons.ts:1336`, rendered through the shared bullet-shape seam (`_shard` in `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts`).
- Code-drawn lime fan icon (`drawShardSwarmIcon`, `src/powerups/icons.ts:1121`).

Missing:
- **No fire SFX.** `playWeaponFireSound()` (`src/audio/effects.ts:628`) has no `shard_swarm` case, so it falls through to the `default:` no-op — the weapon fires silently in live play, in the hold-full metronome and in every gym.
- **No muzzle flash.** The definition declares no `muzzleFlash` metadata, and `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts:896`) only spawns the launch cue `if (def.muzzleFlash)`.
- **No per-weapon impact feedback.** No `impactFx` spec, so `CombatScene.resolveWeaponImpactFx()` returns early: no baked hit cue (the impact is silent) and only the generic warm-white flash (`spawnBulletImpact`, `0xfff2a0`, r7, `CombatScene.ts:434`) rather than a lime shard-coloured one. The fan therefore reads as weak noise against the neon background at 0.72× bullet scale.

## Goal (user story)

As a player holding the Shard Swarm, I want an audible launch and hit so I can hear that the five-shard fan is firing and connecting, and I want the shards and their impacts to punch clearly against the neon field, so the weapon feels as distinctive in the hand as its silhouette suggests — without any change to its balance.

## Scope

`shard_swarm` only. Feel/visual/audio only — no behaviour or balance change: fire rate (750 ms, once per beat), the five offsets (±15°, ±7.5°, 0°), bullet lifetime (0.55 s → ~193 px reach), speed, size and colour stay exactly as they are.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Audible fire.** `playWeaponFireSound('shard_swarm')` routes to a new baked ToneForge fire cue (recipe `aihell-shard-swarm-fire`, rendered by `scripts/build-audio.sh`), so live fire, the hold-full metronome and gym fire all sound identical through the one shared path (`src/audio/effects.ts`, `PLAYER_WEAPON_IMPACT_CUES`-adjacent registry pattern).
- **Audible, visibly distinct impact.** `shard_swarm` declares an `impactFx` spec (`color` = lime-family, `radius`, `duration`, `cue`) resolved through `CombatScene.resolveWeaponImpactFx()`, producing a lime-tinted impact flash and a new baked hit cue (`aihell-shard-swarm-impact`) so the game and every gym connect identically. The generic white fallback flash no longer applies to this weapon.
- **Muzzle flash + more noticeable in-flight VFX.** The definition declares `muzzleFlash` metadata (lime, sized for a five-shard burst) spawned through the shared `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` → `spawnMuzzleFlash` path, and the shards are made more legible in flight (e.g. slightly stronger rim/spine contrast and/or a brighter trail) through the shared `bulletVisuals` seam — no per-scene copies, no new bespoke rendering path.
- **Gym↔game parity.** All changes land in the shared core/seams (`src/utils/weapons.ts`, `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts`, `src/vfx/`, `src/audio/`) and are consumed identically by `PlayScene`, `GymWeapons` and `GymWeaponLeveling`; `CombatScene.equivalence` and the gym-parity/documentation roster guards pass unchanged.
- **Docs + audio catalogue updated.** `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` records both new cues with their recipes and seeds, `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` lists them, and the per-weapon visual roster guards (`src/utils/weaponVisualRoster.docs.test.ts`, `src/utils/bulletVisualRoster.test.ts`) plus README/GDD §4.4/§7.3 per-weapon notes include the Shard Swarm's fire and impact identity instead of listing it as visual-only.
- **No new legibility regressions.** The five-shard fan at full upgrade levels (extra projectiles, larger bullets) must not become a screen-filling blur: the impact/muzzle flashes are rate-limited by the natural 750 ms cadence and the effect sizes stay within the existing per-weapon effect budget.
- **Full test suite passes**, including new/updated tests for the fire cue dispatch, `impactFx` resolution, muzzle-flash spawn, and the audio cue contract test (`src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts`).

## Key files

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `shard_swarm` `muzzleFlash` / `impactFx` metadata
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — ensure the new metadata survives level resolution
- `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts` — in-flight `shard` legibility for the player weapon
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playWeaponFireSound` case + impact cue registry + `playShardSwarm*Sound` exports
- `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-shard-swarm-{fire,impact}.yaml`, `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — shared spawn/impact seams (consume-only; no new hook needed if the metadata path suffices)
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`, README, GDD §4.4 / §7.3

## Known sibling gap (not in this item's scope)

The same missing feel package (`muzzleFlash`, `impactFx`, fire cue) applies to the other four net-new unlock-pool weapons from AH-0MVCRC52P001YIPW: `rear_guard`, `broadside`, `railgun`, `heavy_slug`. Railgun SFX is already tracked by Railgun needs SFX (AH-0MVMIGVCE004VSNA); the remaining three have no item yet. The metadata/pipeline work here should be structured so those can reuse it unchanged.

## Risks / notes

- ToneForge assets are baked, not runtime-synthesised (`src/audio/thrusterShim.ts` is the sole runtime exception): new cues need recipe YAML + a `scripts/build-audio.sh` run, and the seeds must be recorded.
- Audio must remain a safe no-op in headless tests (no audio context).

# Capture crashes on long full-run clips: Playwright CDP pipe overflows (ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG)

## Problem statement

A multi-clip, full-run `npm run capture` (5 clips, `--max-duration 1800000`)
aborts ~23% into a clip (407.5 s of a 1800 s cap) with Playwright's CDP
transport blowing past Node's maximum string length: the browser side of the
`--remote-debugging-pipe` sent more than ~512 MB of bytes with no `\0` message
delimiter, so `PipeTransport._dispatch` throws `ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG`, the
process dies on an unhandled stack, and the hours of wall clock already spent
are lost (nothing is flushed to disk — chunks are only concatenated after the
run ends).

## Users

Primary user: the developer/agent producing long playthrough captures for the
promo/compile pipeline (`npm run capture`, `capture:scenes`, `compile:promo`).

- As the person producing a full 30-minute playthrough, I want the capture to
  either finish or fail with an actionable message and keep whatever was
  recorded, so that a long run is never a total loss.
- As a maintainer, I want capture memory to stay bounded as run length grows,
  so that raising `--max-duration` or batching clips cannot OOM the process.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Root cause identified with evidence.** A diagnostic run (instrumented CDP
   message sizes and `MediaRecorder` `dataavailable` chunk sizes) is captured
   and recorded on this item as a comment: the largest observed CDP message and
   the class of message that overflows (e.g. oversized `Runtime.bindingCalled`
   base64 payload, console/error event, browser logging), plus the observed
   node peak RSS and page-side heap at failure time.
2. **Bounded memory, streaming write.** Node writes recorder chunks to the
   output file as they arrive instead of accumulating them for the whole run;
   peak node RSS for a full-cap run stays under a documented budget (target
   < 512 MB, measured with `process.memoryUsage().rss`) and no single in-memory
   buffer exceeds the configured chunk cap. Verified by a unit test driving the
   sink with simulated chunks totalling more than the CDP budget.
3. **Bounded page-side memory.** The page no longer retains every recorded
   `Blob` for the whole run (or the retained prefix is capped/drained), so page
   heap also stays bounded for a 30-minute recording. Verified by a unit test
   over the page-side recorder script.
4. **Oversized-payload guard.** A single chunk payload above a configured cap
   is rejected before it can reach the pipe, with an actionable error naming
   the payload size, the cap and the recorder state (rather than a raw
   `Buffer.toString` stack). Verified by a unit test.
5. **Graceful failure with salvage.** Any pipe/browser/recorder failure results
   in: the bytes already streamed are kept, a `<stem>.partial.webm` (or
   equivalent documented path) is left behind and reported, exactly one
   actionable message is printed first, and the CLI exits non-zero. Verified by
   a test that injects a browser-side failure mid-recording.
6. **Probe and sidecars unchanged in contract.** The end-of-clip probe
   (resolution, duration, non-black fraction, colour variety, motion, audio
   peak/RMS) and the `.action.jsonl` / `.capture.json` exports still work after
   the change, and the `--json` result shape plus exit codes are unchanged.
   Verified by the existing capture tests passing unmodified (plus additions).
7. **Both capture paths use the fix.** The single/batch clip path and the
   `capture:scenes` path consume the same shared chunk-sink/probe helpers —
   no divergent copy of the recording plumbing.
8. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` (cost-of-long-runs / known
   limits / new flags or partial-output behaviour), the README where capture
   flags are documented, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes (run through the
   test skill), including the new tests covering criteria 2–5.

## Constraints

- **Evidence before fix.** The overflowing message class must be pinned down;
  a speculative "increase buffers" change is not acceptable.
- **Artefact contract preserved.** One WebM per clip plus the existing sidecars;
  `--json` shape, probe verdicts and exit codes stay backward compatible.
- **No new runtime dependencies**, no `src/` gameplay changes (this is dev
  tooling; `scripts/check-bundle-hygiene.mjs` must keep passing).
- **Playwright stays on the pinned version** — a workaround must not require a
  Playwright upgrade (an upgrade may be a separate chore item if it is the only
  fix).
- **Gym↔game parity is out of scope** (no gameplay behaviour changes).
- **No CI wiring of long captures**: wall-clock long-run verification stays a
  manual/soak check reported on this item, not a CI test.

## Existing state

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` (~2.7k lines) records via `canvas.captureStream(60)`
  → `MediaRecorder` (`recorder.start(1000)`, 8 Mbps, `--max-duration` default
  1800 s from `scripts/capture-run-lifecycle.mjs`).
- Chunk plumbing is duplicated in two places with the same shape:
  `page.exposeFunction('__aiHellCaptureChunk', ...)` at
  `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs:1457` (single/batch clip) and `:1900`
  (`--scenes` path, one recorder over many scenes), each pushing
  `Buffer.from(base64, 'base64')` into an in-memory `chunks` array that is
  `Buffer.concat`-ed only after the recorder stops (`:1598`, `:2024`).
- The page also keeps every chunk Blob: `chunks.push(event.data)` inside
  `startRecording`'s `ondataavailable`, consumed at the end by
  `stopRecordingAndProbe` as `new Blob(chunks)` → `blob.arrayBuffer()` (audio
  decode) and an object URL for the `<video>` probe.
- At 8 Mbps an 1800 s run is ≈1.8 GB of WebM, i.e. ≈1.8 GB in node buffers
  **and** ≈1.8 GB of page Blobs, plus a full `blob.arrayBuffer()` copy in the
  probe — all before anything is written to disk.
- Failure signature: `ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG` from
  `playwright-core/lib/server/pipeTransport.js:67` (`_dispatch` concatenating
  `_pendingBuffers` and calling `.toString()`), raised at ~407 s into the clip,
  after four earlier clips in the same process had completed.

## Desired change

1. **Diagnose** the overflowing CDP message (instrument the transport/payload
   sizes; check whether it is the per-second `Runtime.bindingCalled` base64
   upload, a console/pageerror event, or browser-side output on the pipe).
2. **Stream to disk**: replace the in-memory `chunks` array with a chunk sink
   that appends each decoded chunk to the output file as it arrives (single and
   scenes paths), so memory is O(one chunk) rather than O(duration).
3. **Bound the page side**: stop retaining all Blobs (drain/limit the retained
   prefix) and let the probe read from the streamed file rather than an
   ever-growing in-page Blob, keeping audio peak/RMS and frame sampling intact.
4. **Guard and fail well**: cap individual payloads before they reach the pipe;
   wrap capture so a transport failure reports one actionable message, keeps
   the `*.partial.webm` bytes and exits non-zero.
5. **Document** the new behaviour and the measured long-run budget.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — chunk plumbing at `:1457`/`:1900`, the
  `chunks` accumulation at `:1598`/`:2024`, `startRecording` and
  `stopRecordingAndProbe` (page-side retention), top-of-file pipeline docs.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — existing capture tests; new sink/guard/
  failure-path tests live here or alongside the new module.
- `scripts/capture-chunk-sink.mjs` (+ `.d.mts`, `.test.ts`, **new**) — bounded
  chunk sink: decode base64 → append to file, payload cap, partial-artefact
  bookkeeping, peak-bytes accounting.
- `scripts/capture-run-lifecycle.mjs` — where the duration/tail constants live;
  a chunk-cap constant may belong here for single-source reuse.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — cost-of-long-runs, known limits, streaming/
  partial-output behaviour, diagnostics.
- `README.md` — capture flag/behaviour summary if anything user-visible changes.
- `scripts/check-bundle-hygiene.mjs` — only if any dev marker is added (must
  keep passing, no change expected).

## Risks & assumptions

- **The overflow may be browser-side, not ours.** If diagnosis shows Chromium
  writing non-CDP output into the debugging pipe (crashpad/logging), the fix is
  a launch-flag/guard workaround plus the same bounded-memory work; the item
  stays valid either way.
- **WebM chunk concatenation is assumed valid** (already relied on by the
  in-page `new Blob(chunks)` and node's `Buffer.concat`); streaming appends must
  be verified to produce a decodable file via the existing probe.
- **Probe rework risk.** Moving the probe off the in-page Blob is the least
  obvious part; if it cannot be done without a new dependency (ffprobe), keep
  the in-page decode for clips below a size threshold and record the rest as a
  child item rather than widening this one.
- **Not reproducible on demand.** A 30-minute soak is expensive; the unit-level
  sink tests must prove the bound without it, with one manual soak reported.
- **Scope-creep risk:** gaps found while diagnosing (e.g. telemetry buffer
  growth, series artefact size) are recorded as `discovered-from` items unless
  they block this fix.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK** – Spike: automated gameplay video capture (headless
  browser + scripted bot) — origin of the pipeline.
- **AH-0MUXZ4DDV0098ZW4** – Document full-run capture and dwell — documents the
  full-run path and `--max-duration`.
- **AH-0MUX2K8U7000GFNU** – Create full video playthroughs — the consumer use
  case for long clips.
- Docs: `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` (§ Cost of long runs, § Known limits),
  `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` (§7.5 join anchor), `docs/TELEMETRY.md`.
- Automated related-work report: `- **Q:** (Pre-check, not asked of the producer) Does this item need planning?
  — **Answer (plan skill, `plan_helpers.py plan-if-needed`):** yes,
  `decision: plan`, effort Small / risk Medium. Source: plan_helpers output,
  plan session 2026-10-25.
- **Q:** (Approval gate, not asked of the producer) Does the feature plan need
  producer approval? — **Answer (plan skill, `plan_helpers.py
  plan-approval-gate`):** no — `request_approval: false`; the gate only
  requires approval for Extra Large effort **and** High/Severe risk. Source:
  plan_helpers output, plan session 2026-10-25.
- **Q:** Which probe fallback should the plan assume if a streamed-file probe
  cannot preserve audio peak/RMS? — **Answer (recorded assumption, existing
  appendix above):** keep the existing in-page decode for clips below a
  documented size threshold and file any residual gap as a child item rather
  than adding a dependency such as ffprobe. Source: this item, "Risks &
  assumptions" §Probe rework risk.
- **Q:** Should the fix include bounded memory or only a guard? — **Already
  answered** above (bounded memory is inherent to the reported failure); not
  re-asked. Source: this item's Appendix.

## Related work (automated report)` section
  appended by the find-related skill.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Is the failing invocation a batch of full-run clips or a single clip?
  — **Answer (operator's report):** a 5-clip batch (`Capturing clip 5/5`) with
  the default full-run path, cap 1800 s. Source: pasted console output.
- **Q:** Should the fix minimise scope (guard + actionable error only) or also
  make long-run memory bounded? — **No clarifying question was required:**
  bounded memory is inherent to the reported failure (≈1.8 GB buffered per
  side for a 30-minute run), so streaming is in scope. If the producer prefers
  a pure guard, that is a plan-time decision the ACs can be narrowed against.
  Source: repo inspection of `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` (`chunks`
  accumulation, `Buffer.concat` at the end).
- **Q:** Is a Playwright/Chromium upgrade acceptable as the fix? —
  **Assumption recorded:** no; stay on the pinned version and treat an upgrade
  as a separate chore item unless diagnosis proves it is the only fix.
- **Q:** Does the probe need to keep its current in-page decode implementation?
  — **Assumption recorded:** the probe's *contract* (verdicts, audio peak/RMS,
  frame samples) must be preserved; its implementation may move to reading the
  streamed file, with any residual gap filed as a child item.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK** – Spike: automated gameplay video capture (headless browser + scripted bot) (completed)
- **AH-0MUX2K8U7000GFNU** – Create full video playthroughs (completed)
- **AH-0MUXZ4DDV0098ZW4** – Document full-run capture and dwell (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — matched: actionable, aihellcapture, aihellcapturechunk, also, artefacts (+111 more)
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — matched: actionable, aihellcapture, also, artefacts, batch (+103 more)
- `README.md` — matched: accumulates, actionable, aihellcapture, also, batch (+102 more)

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-10-25)

Nine features, in dependency order (all children created with
`--stage intake_complete` and blocking edges wired via `wl dep add`):

| # | Feature | Kind | Parent ACs |
|---|---------|------|------------|
| 1 | Diagnose the overflowing CDP message with instrumentation (AH-0MVNT25JI004OVKQ) | verification | AC1 |
| 2 | Stream recorder chunks to disk through a bounded sink (AH-0MVNT26AQ005LDNS) | impl (TDD) | AC2 |
| 3 | Bound page-side recorder Blob retention (AH-0MVNT274M009XRJ1) | impl (TDD) | AC3 |
| 4 | Split and cap oversized chunk payloads before the pipe (AH-0MVNT27XR0080I3C) | impl (TDD) | AC4 |
| 5 | Probe long clips from the streamed file, contract preserved (AH-0MVNT28SJ008ZHDB) | impl (TDD) | AC3, AC6 |
| 6 | Graceful failure with salvage of streamed bytes (AH-0MVNT29MC008BQPY) | impl (TDD) | AC5 |
| 7 | Unify recording plumbing across both capture paths (AH-0MVNT2AFI00639N3) | impl (TDD) | AC7 |
| 8 | Document streaming, caps, partial output and long-run budget (AH-0MVNT2BBV008C4HT) | docs | AC8 |
| 9 | Verify fix with full suite and a manual long-run soak (AH-0MVNT2CD3001I8ES) | verification | AC6, AC9 |

Dependency spine: diagnosis gates every code item (the **evidence before fix**
constraint); the sink gates the payload guard, the probe and the salvage item;
unification comes after the sink/guard/retention/probe/salvage so the shared
shape is settled once; docs and the soak/suite verification come last.

### Vertical slice assessment

Every code feature is an end-to-end slice on its own terms — a new or extracted
module, its wiring into *both* capture paths, and its hermetic test, delivered
together (test-first inside each item). The single consolidated docs item is
deliberate rather than a horizontal layer: the numbers the docs must publish
(measured RSS/page heap, chosen caps, partial-output path) only exist after
items 1–7 land. The final verification item is the phase gate for the manual
soak and the full suite, which the parent explicitly keeps out of CI.

### Guidance between phases

Before starting each item, re-read it and its dependencies and update its
description if the preceding item changed the shared shape (cap constants, sink
API, probe source). Items 4, 5, 6 and 7 are the ones most likely to need a
description refresh after item 2 lands.

### Automated review stages (plan skill step 6)

1. **Requirements & AC alignment** — every parent AC (1–9) maps to at least one
   child AC; no invented requirements beyond the parent's own stated fallbacks
   (size-threshold probe fallback, `discovered-from` escape hatch).
2. **Completeness** — each child has goal, context, acceptance criteria and
   `**Key Files:**`; every key-file path validated syntactically
   (`validate_key_files_format` reports no issues for all nine children).
3. **Sequencing & dependencies** — diagnosis first (evidence), TDD inside each
   code item, unification after the code items, docs/verification last; every
   edge wired with `wl dep add` and no cycles.
4. **Scope sizing** — each item is one deliverable; the two riskier items (the
   streamed probe and the diagnostics soak) carry explicit escape hatches so
   they cannot silently widen.
5. **Acceptance & testability** — every code AC names the hermetic test that
   proves it; no browser or Vite server is needed for any unit AC.
6. **Polish & handoff** — descriptions name the exact files and line anchors of
   the duplicated plumbing, so an implementer needs no re-discovery.

### Open questions (non-blocking)

- **OPEN QUESTION (producer):** the exact in-page probe threshold and the
  bounded audio-prefix cap are left to item 5 with a documented default; if the
  streamed audio decode proves unreliable, is falling back to the existing
  in-page decode for clips under a threshold acceptable (the parent's recorded
  assumption says yes)?
- **OPEN QUESTION (producer):** item 6 uses `<stem>.partial.webm` as the
  salvage path because the parent's AC5 names it; confirm that naming, and that
